text:
alejandro: Heads-up — seeing a ~25% throughput dip and memory spikes on the NF4/FP4 rollout in eu-west-1 canary, started ~09:10 UTC.

riley: saw perf alert, stack trace shows kernel swap churn + a bunch of host memcpy.

cheng: is this the new mini-quant kernel selector? we pushed a heuristic change that prefers smaller kernels for short sequences.

alejandro: yes, selector bumped to 'miniquanta' policy last night for canary. suspect it picks an INT4-compatible kernel that ends up forcing host fallback on mixed-batch sizes.

runtime-bot: Canary telemetry snapshot (09:12): p50 latency +18%, p99 +62%, avg tokens/sec -24%, host_mem_copies +37%.

maria: quick profiling dump attached below — looks like KV cache eviction spikes coincide with the kernel swap window.

riley: paste profiler snippet:
```
[09:11:58] kernel_load nf4_fp4_small -> nf4_fp4_large (3x)
[09:11:59] KV_CACHE_EVICT user=svc-42 count=12 size=1.8GiB
[09:12:00] host_memcpy 0.8s / token_batch
[09:12:01] scheduler_preempt small_batch -> microbatch
```

dave: microbatches are killing batching efficiency. miniquanta selector seems to choose a kernel that requires a different KV layout so we copy out/in more often.

cheng: re: calibration — did we use the new TF32 fallback threshold? last sweep adjusted quant thresholds which can change kernel compatibility.

alejandro: yes, calibration tweak from yesterday lowered dynamic range margin for NF4 so more tensors quantize to the compact layout. Good for memory but apparently incompatible with the 'streaming' kernel path.

maria: hypothesis: calibration -> different weight packing -> selector chooses compact kernel -> compact kernel can't share KV layout with legacy streaming code -> runtime does host-side conversion -> memcpy spike -> throughput drop.

ops: can we confirm by forcing the packing to legacy variant? any quick flag to disable compact packing in canary?

riley: there's a runtime flag: --quant-packing=legacy|compact. I'll toggle on one host in canary and run smoke.

runtime-bot: Action taken: Riley toggled --quant-packing=legacy on pool gpu-canary-7 at 09:20 UTC. Telemetry will emit in ~2m.

alejandro: also try pinning kernel selection to the previous kernel_id for a subset (selector.override kernel_id=0x4a). if throughput returns we confirm selector regression.

riley: pinned kernel on canary-7, running synthetic workload (seq_len=64, batch shapes mixed).

runtime-bot: Canary telemetry snapshot (09:23): p50 latency -5% (vs baseline), tokens/sec +19%, host_mem_copies -82%.

cheng: that looks like strong signal. pinning + legacy packing fixes it. root cause likely interplay between calibration changes and selector heuristics.

maria: follow-up: we should add a selector compatibility matrix so selector chooses kernels that share KV memory layouts with streaming path. current greedy speed-first heuristic ignores KV layout cost.

dave: +1. Also add a telemetry counter for kernel_layout_mismatch that increments when runtime does host-convert. We had a proxy in host_mem_copy but explicit counter helps alerts.

alejandro: immediate mitigation: roll back the selector change for canary and hold calibration thresholds until we run a matrix test. I'll open a PR to revert the selector change.

riley: opened PR #1429 — rollback miniquanta policy. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for review.

ops: scheduling a quick postmortem doc and a short sync 09:45 UTC to decide next steps (calibration sweep with layout-aware constraints).

maria: notes for postmortem: include microbenchmark (seq_len 1/8/64/512), batch-mixing patterns, KV usage, packing variant, selector decision logs. capture kernel_id transitions timestamps.

cheng: long-term: during quant calibration, emit a 'layout_compatibility_signature' per quant config so selector can match. avoids runtime host-conversions.

alejandro: agreed. also add a canary test that exercises mixed-batch shapes every release. current canary didn't stress the microbatch path.

riley: I'll add telemetry events for: kernel_selected:<id>, packing_variant:<compact|legacy>, kv_layout_hash:<hex>.

runtime-bot: Task created: ENG-RUNTIME-319 add telemetry + selector fallback. Assigned: Riley, ETA: 3d.

dave: temporary action items: revert selector on all canary pools, pin kernel for affected hosts, enable legacy packing for affected model family.

alejandro: thanks team. sync in 20m. will dump full perf logs + profiling artifact to the incident doc. :thumbsup:

riley: one last note — this showed how calibration-for-quality can regress perf if layout info isn't propagated. remind ML folks to include runtime constraints in calibration PRs.

maria: noted; will draft contributor checklist for calibration changes.

ops: meeting invite sent.

alejandro: closing notes: root cause = calibration packing change + greedy kernel selector ignoring KV layout -> host conversions -> memcpy spike -> throughput drop. Mitigation = rollback selector + legacy packing + telemetry. Follow-ups = layout signature, selector compatibility matrix, canary stress test.
